availability_inventory.scope: Direct public callable names; not overall compatibility

limits: Object, structured and variable-width StringDType arrays remain unavailable
Non-native numeric endian remains unavailable
Python subclasses, complete warnings and exception-class fidelity are not claimed
Availability inventory alone verifies no full behavior; alternate Lua spellings can exist
Earlier take/choose differences remain separate; full NumPy parity is not claimed
All eighteen scoped FFT callables are available; full FFT behavior, every dtype/length/out alias and device argument remain uncertified
FFT float32/complex64 numeric tolerance: absolute3e-6 plus relative3e-6; wider output2e-12; values/metadata and known precision regression values checked separately
Sampling uses Lua options tables; full NumPy positional/device/array-valued count/warning APIs remain incomplete

Linspace reference values are exact; power/log tolerances follow computation precision before final casts (half2e-3, float32/complex64 3e-6, wider2e-12 absolute+relative); integer/bool/string values remain exact
Shared FMA path and raw-bit extended formatting were executed on Linux x86; other ABI branches, every hardware rounding/unsafe cast and full SIMD dispatch remain uncertified
NumPy float128 uses the existing LuaRay longdouble spelling on the tested x86 ABI; original width/strides are checked

Creation uses Lua options and copy=if_needed to express copy=None; foreign array protocols, device/like dispatch, general subclasses, ndarray-valued shapes and full positional signatures are unsupported
Nested Lua sequences containing ndarrays or temporal scalar userdata are not fully implemented; subok is validated but only the native array class exists
Historical LuaRay np.astype/ndarray:astype numeric-to-generic-datetime rejection remains as an explicit partial compatibility contract; creation uses a separate source-derived raw-array cast path
Empty constructor values are uninitialized; tests compare metadata then perform actual writes before inspecting values
Unary operations return typed zero-dimensional arrays for Lua scalars; this is a Lua return-type adaptation
Only out/where unary options are supported; complete dtype/casting/order/subok/device, ufunc object methods, warning and floating status protocols remain incomplete
Integer reciprocal-zero explicitly follows audited x86 NumPy loops; other ABI and nondefault rounding-mode behavior need separate verification

General complex square/reciprocal tolerance is relative6e-7 for complex64 and2e-15 for wider complex types; thirty-eight FMA layout/writeback cases compare exactly; all observed new numerical errors were zero
Coercion uses the existing constructor; ordinary string-to-numeric table construction and all nested typed-array combinations remain incomplete
Binary ordinary scalar results are typed rank-zero arrays; complete Python scalar classes, foreign inputs and nested array coercion remain incomplete
Fmod compares exactly in new fixtures; float_power and existing power/arctan2/hypot use relative2e-12 tolerance; observed float_power relative error3.2300436499022e-15 and absolute3.1974423109205e-14
String add supports fixed-width S+S and U+U, canonical endian and staged output casts; variable StringDType and mixed S/U are unsupported
Lua raw strings default to Unicode unless paired with an explicit S/U array; separate Python bytes/str scalar classes are not reproduced
Binary logical promotion follows boolean conversion before computation, including tiny weak float/complex scalars and fixed-width strings; unary logical_not has separate supported signatures
Layout values, metadata, sharing, actual writable status and post-write backing states compare exactly in 25134 new cases; empty allocations and reshape views can have distinct strides
Reshape accepts one Lua integer/table shape plus C/F/A and copy=true/false/if_needed; full historical NumPy variadic shape signatures, device/subclass/foreign protocols remain incomplete
Ravel/flatten K-order preserves negative logical traversal and stable zero-stride ambiguity; all host ABI/foreign malformed array layouts are not certified
Reshape copy=false applies after ordinary Lua inputs are coerced to a temporary array; this differs from asarray copy=false, which forbids its own necessary allocation
Component real/imag views preserve typed storage and identity; direct ndarray.real/imag property replacement setters remain unsupported; write through the returned view instead
Root real/imag ordinary scalar results follow the typed rank-zero ndarray convention; full Python scalar/subclass/device protocols remain incomplete
Reality predicates distinguish values from dtype; value results are typed bool arrays while object predicates return Lua booleans
Real_if_close supports weak Lua numeric/integer/boolean tolerances; nil means default100; ndarray-valued tolerances and complete Python argument protocols remain unsupported
Real_if_close casts tolerance at component precision, scales tol>1 by epsilon and compares strictly; exact x87 boundary references are built via real native ldexp/stack/component writes
Legacy Lua astype string conversions follow ndarray.astype rather than NumPy root Array API numeric-only signature; complex strings round through two doubles even for clongdouble

Complex text parsing now accepts valid overflow/underflow and rejects malformed underscores, C hexadecimal/nan-payload syntax and embedded NUL in nonboolean numeric strings; full Unicode decimal/space grammar and locale-independent parsing remain pending
Round preserves typed composition, complex component assignment and root TypeError retry; Lua errors remain ordinary Lua errors rather than Python exception objects
Internal ln_error gained a category field; development-version C consumers must rebuild all native objects; full error-class coverage is not certified
Power-of-ten uses source multiplication order through308 and stabilized infinity from309; INT_MIN/MAX native bounds tested without executing upstream billion-step loops

Floating timedelta multiply/divide uses the source double loop including longdouble coefficients and x86 NaT overflow results; integer division, timedelta ratios and complete temporal arithmetic remain unimplemented
Round Lua options/typed scalar return adaptation and constructor limits remain; every subclass/device/foreign protocol, FP status/rounding mode and host ABI is not certified
Clip supports positional bounds and out/where options; Python keyword aliases and dtype/casting/order/signature/subok are not accepted
Clip resolves strong descriptor categories before weak value packing, implements integer-bound elision and fused numeric/time loops; complete foreign DType and scalar protocols remain unavailable

Uniform non-reduction buffer cost planning is currently selected for clip, using the source default8192; Python setbufsize, every possible memory layout, warnings, NaN payloads and host floating environment remain uncertified
View reinterprets supported descriptor bytes and shares the owner; changing itemsize follows last-axis contiguity/divisibility, with scalar/singleton/empty rules and overflow checks
Tobytes exports actual bytes including padding; NumPy2.5.3 K uses C order for numeric/bytes/time but KEEPORDER ravel for Unicode; letters case-insensitive, Lua nil/default C
View accepts dtype strings only; Python subclasses/type arguments, void/subarray/structured/object/variableStringDType and non-native numeric endian remain unsupported

Alignment flags and scalar loads/stores plus generic/legacy iterators and core reduction/accumulation staging support directed unaligned cases; every downstream algorithm and foreign storage layout is not certified
Frozen raw-byte oracles use little-endian x86-64; independently constructed longdouble padding and all foreign ABIs are not certified

Cross follows NumPy2.5.3 three-component inputs, common-dtype casts and output-last allocation plus axis view; positive Lua axes are one-based and root ordinary array-like inputs use the existing constructor

General complex cross budgets are fixed at6e-7 for complex64 and2e-15 for wider complex, scaled by max(1,abs(component)); exact state/metadata/zero/nonfinite cases are separate; byte-identical CPU FMA dispatch is not certified

Meshgrid uses an explicit Lua input sequence table and returns a sequence table; copy/sparse require Lua booleans; indexing is xy/ij; Python variadic/custom protocols and warning objects are not reproduced

Meshgrid copy=false preserves source writable/readonly broadcasting and may share inputs or other cells; incompatible input flattening can still copy; inferred reshape preserves empty/singleton strides
Root diagonal uses the first two axes by default; linalg.diagonal uses the last two; extracted views are read-only
Diagonal extraction uses the native C int offset range; construction uses checked native-size dimensions; foreign index objects and complete Python signature/dispatch fidelity are not implemented

Diagonal index helpers return a Lua sequence of shared one-based index vectors; diag_indices_from requires an actual ndarray with equal-sized axes. Python index/tuple/subclass protocols are not reproduced.

Triangular index helpers return two independent contiguous one-based index vectors; _from requires a two-dimensional ndarray and accepts rectangular matrices. Strict Lua integer and Lua sequence conventions replace Python protocols.

Fill_diagonal uses logical C iteration with live same-dtype aliases, cycling values and Boolean wrap. Lua options and scalar bounds differ from typed unsafe casting; full foreign scalar, subclass and warning protocols are not reproduced.
Kron coerces both inputs to strong arrays, interleaves axes and uses C-order reshape. Scalar-right and scalar-left rank limits differ as in NumPy2.5.3; scalar results are typed rank-zero ndarrays.
General kron random complex64 values use relative3e-7 and wider float/complex relative3e-15; exact ordinary values, signed zeros and metadata are separate. Observed new numerical errors were zero.

Integer duration multiplication uses int64 coefficient conversion, NaT propagation and checked overflow. Completed writes, mask-run continuation and tested buffer/negative-stride traversal match references; every possible foreign/output/iterator layout is not certified.

In176 failed buffered unit-conversion cases, upstream flushes nondeterministic uninitialized suffix cells. Only defined prefix values and full metadata are compared; LuaRay preserves unwritten cells. Full suffix/exception-message parity is not claimed.
Tensordot adapts positive axes to one-based Lua integers and returns typed rank-zero arrays. Negative count means no contraction. Python iterable/subclass protocols remain unsupported.

Tensordot has154 executed object-result cases explicitly blocked, excluded from parity-eligible counts. BLAS result zero signs are not certified across vendors:44 observed sign differences; input zero signs and non-BLAS result zeros remain exact.
General random contraction tolerances are absolute+relative3e-6 for float32/complex64 and2e-12 for wider float/complex types; exact ordinary nonzero values and metadata are separate.
Legacy timedelta dot uses raw int64 wrapping after common-unit conversion and treats NaT as raw bits, matching arraytypes.c.src rather than ordinary duration multiplication.
new_check_semantics: Exact tested input states, metadata, ownership and ordinary nonzero results; bounded general floating contraction errors and counted BLAS zero-sign differences.154 object-result cases are blocked, not compatible.
new_reference_checks_scope: Includes explicit blocked-result checks and exact input-state checks; blocked cases are not counted as compatible.
